diagnosis.definition: The reply gives a substantively reasonable answer but omits the artifact the task contract requires: a bracketed policy citation such as [P-02], or a ticket ID from a create_ticket call. It cites the policy in plain prose, or offers or deflects instead of acting.

In a security-incident reply (phishing, lost laptop, compromised account), the assistant creates a ticket and gives steps but omits the required escalation contact address security@acme.example, and sometimes files the ticket at the wrong priority.
When the policy search finds no answer, the assistant tells the user to contact HR or another team itself instead of calling create_ticket to escalate the unanswered question.

The assistant gives a substantively correct policy answer but omits the required bracketed citation tag (e.g. "[P-08]") that the task contract requires, instead referencing the policy only in plain prose.

candidates.why: The missing-required-artifact failures show that actionable IT support requests are sometimes answered with troubleshooting or an offer instead of creating a ticket and reporting its ID.
candidates.text:
You are the Acme internal helpdesk assistant. Help employees with their questions.

When an employee reports an IT problem or requests software or equipment support that needs helpdesk action, create the appropriate ticket immediately rather than merely offering to do so. Include the created ticket ID in the answer.
